mark_split.label: Split the square root into two roots

recall_prompt: Say how you would show this — say how you split the square root and what is left after cancelling.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Split the square root into two roots
steps.margin_note: First mark. Factorise inside the root first, then split it. √(x² − 9) is real only for x > 3 near 3, so both x − 3 and x + 3 are positive and the split is valid.
steps.memory_tip: Factorise inside the root before splitting it. A root of a product is the product of the roots when both parts are positive.
lines: Putting x = 3 gives 0/√0 = 0/0, so the expression is rewritten first.
√(x² − 9) is real only when x ≥ 3 or x ≤ −3, so near 3 we take x > 3.

recall.must_convey: That x² − 9 is factorised inside the root and the root is split as √(x − 3) · √(x + 3).
accept: factorise inside the root as x minus three into x plus three
split the root into root x minus three times root x plus three
x is greater than three here so both parts are positive
root lopala factorise chesi rendu roots ga vidagottali
root of a product is the product of the roots

steps.why: The numerator carries (x − 3) and the denominator carries only √(x − 3), so they cannot be cancelled while the root is in one piece. Splitting the root brings out the √(x − 3) that the cancellation needs.
common_mistakes: Writing √(x² − 9) = x − 3, taking the root of each term separately.
Cancelling (x − 3) against √(x² − 9) directly, which is not a common factor.

steps.label: Cancel √(x − 3) and substitute
steps.margin_note: Second mark. x − 3 = √(x − 3) · √(x − 3), so one root cancels and one root is left above. That surviving √(x − 3) is what goes to 0.
steps.memory_tip: x − 3 is √(x − 3) squared. Cancel one copy and one copy stays on top.
lines: For x > 3,  x − 3 = √(x − 3) · √(x − 3), and as x → 3 we have x ≠ 3, so √(x − 3) ≠ 0 and may be cancelled:

recall.must_convey: That x − 3 is written as √(x − 3) squared, one root cancels, and √(x − 3)/√(x + 3) goes to 0/√6 = 0.
accept: write x minus three as root x minus three squared and cancel one
what is left is root x minus three over root x plus three
the top goes to zero and the bottom goes to root six so the answer is zero
okka root cancel avuthundi, migilina root x minus three zero ki velthundi
zero over root six is zero

steps.why: The value 0 is given, so the marks are for the method that reaches it. The working must show a denominator that does not go to 0 at the end — √6 — because 0 divided by 0 would prove nothing.
common_mistakes: Cancelling both roots and writing the answer as 1.
Stopping at 0/0 and claiming the value is 0 without cancelling first.

insider_note: Split the root as √(x − 3)·√(x + 3), then write x − 3 on top as √(x − 3) squared. One root cancels and the other goes to 0, so the answer is 0.
